item.title: Silakut Live from the Floe Edge
item.description: Silakut Live from the Floe Edge is LIVE TVSilakut Series Episodes present the LIVE footage filmed in the Igloolik area, broadcast live in May and August 2019, edited into 10 episodes. Zacharias Kunuk discusses with people from five Baffin Island communities the expansion of the Mary River Mine. They meet up to play string games, hunt, talk about their campsites, tell stories of their youth, and voice their opinions of the mine. item.title: The Isuma Book
item.description: The Isuma Book is an iterative online publication. item.description: Co-Director Zacharias Kunuk writes, “First day we all leave – five boats from Ham Bay. And right away the boat, that we later lost, started to have a motor problems. But at the end of the first day we were going through the straits with moving ice, but we all camped that first night near the cabin on the island. item.title: One day in the life of Noah Piugattuk
item.description: One Day in the Life of Noah Piugattuk compresses Piugattuk’s 96-year lifetime into a dramatized feature film portrait of one day in that life, a 24-hour day when the sun never sets, out hunting seals on the spring sea ice in May 1961, in the Igloolik region of north Baffin Island.Noah Piugattuk was born in 1900 when Igloolik Inuit still lived as they had for four millennia – self-sufficient and self-sustained, as if they were the only people on earth. item.title: Isuma Video on Demand
item.description: Isuma’s exhibition in cyberspace presents a collection of Isuma and other indigenous-language films, including Atanarjuat The Fast Runner (Cannes Camera d’Or 2001); The Journals of Knud Rasmussen (opening film at 2006 Toronto International Film Festival); Before Tomorrow (by Igloolik’s Arnait women’s collective); Edge of the Knife, the world’s first feature film in the Haida language; and One Day in the Life of Noah Piugattuk. item.title: Tunnganarniq Nunagijavut
item.description: Tunnganariq Nunagijavut (Welcome to Where We Live Now) is a weekly, live cultural and current affairs series produced in-house by Uvagut TV with community partners throughout Inuit Nunangat.The series launched in June 2021 and broadcasts live on Uvagut TV. Community hosts welcome a variety of guests and explore contemporary issues and themes. item.title: ᓇᖕᒥᓂᖅᐳᑦ ᐃᓄᐃᑦ TV | Authentic Inuit TV
item.description: Uvagut TV (meaning “Our” TV) is Canada’s first 24/7 Inuktut television channel. Uvagut TV broadcasts children’s shows, movies, documentaries, cultural and current affairs programming in Inuktut to communities across the north and throughout the country.Uvagut TV connects and empowers Inuit to share stories with one another; ensures children are growing up with television programming in their own language; and informs Inuit about issues affecting their lands, lives and culture.
